title: iparapheur captures the signature but keeps the approval record in a mutable application
content:
iparapheur is an electronic approval circuit for French local government: documents follow a defined route and are signed at the points that require it. The signature is captured. The surrounding record — that this person approved, in this role, on this delegation — lives in the application's own mutable store.

The research frames the collectivité's question in exactly the terms this project is built around: who approved, under which delegation, and can it be replayed years later. Delegation is what makes mutability expensive. Signing authority in local government is delegated and re-delegated over time, so a store that holds only the current arrangement cannot explain why a signature made three years ago was valid when it was made.

The replay horizon compounds the problem, because approvals have to stay defensible long after the application has been upgraded, migrated or replaced. Libriciel is a cooperative building for that constituency, which means the requirement reaches them as an obligation from their clients rather than as a feature idea of their own.
